answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-rate-limit gate: every new agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed for misbehavior. Picture the economy as a meadow with a single narrow inlet — thousands of fake identities can crowd the inlet, but only those willing to risk real value pass through. Like a falcon that can only strike one target per dive, honest peers can attest only a few newcomers per round, so a flood of cheap sybils stalls at the gate while genuine agents accumulate reputation. Forgery becomes unprofitable.
